I q39 a8 p318b.text: Hence we see that an image is said to be beautiful, if it perfectly represents even an ugly thing.

transcription.reason: Human transcription from the printed 1912 page; the OCR is not used as the text.
transcription.original_text: Hence we see that an image is said to be beautiful, if it perfectly represents even an ugly thing.

I q39 a8 p318b.alignment: The complete sentence corresponds to the Latin: an image may be called beautiful if it perfectly represents even an ugly thing.

Independently inspected the Latin 1894 p. 318 and English 1912 p. 144. The 19-word sentence and its punctuation match the page and preserve the claim that an image can be beautiful when it perfectly represents even an ugly thing. Neither printed sentence carries special emphasis. Oxford scholarship identifies Laurence Shapcote as translator of the Dominican version.

mexico_quotation.assessment: Independent reader examined LFDA article 148(I) and this 19-word sentence in the comparative research context. The complete sentence is short relative to the work and does not substitute for it; the published wording and attribution must remain intact. The precise context and Mexican transitional term must be assessed separately; this is not a claim that the translation is in the Mexican public domain.
